  PROPOSED BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020-21

  This report provides a summary of the Proposed Budget and Capital Improvement
  Plan (CIP) for Fiscal Year 2020-21. The operating budget is balanced, with revenues
  totaling $70,850,202 and expenditures totaling $69,369,166. The CIP totals
  $6,191,594, providing new/additional funding for 16 projects.

  Recommendations:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report. The Public
  Hearing for the Budget is scheduled for June 2, 2020 at which time staff will seek City
  Council recommendations on any changes prior to adoption.

  3. ADJOURNMENT

MINUTES OF MAY 12, 2020, 5:30 P.M.
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
5:31 p.m. on Tuesday, May 12, 2020, with all Council Members and staff participating by
teleconference.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux,  Assistant  City  Manager/Community
  Development Director Arminé Chaparyan, Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Rebecca
  Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk
  Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  and Interim Finance Director Kenneth Louie.

Mayor Menchaca provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
submit comments.

1. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Doug Richter, resident, provided comments on his opposition to the City subsidizing
  the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce.

  Senya Lubisich, Chair of the Historic Preservation and Cultural Resources Commission
  and resident, and Chuck Myers, resident, provided comments requesting that the
  proposed funding for Historic Preservation Ordinance be retained in the 2020-2021
  Budget.
CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 3  May 12, 2020
 2. STUDY SESSION

  PROPOSED BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020-21

  City Manager Lazzaretto introduced Management Specialist Julia James and thanked
  staff for their contributions, gave an overview of the proposed Budget, explained that
  a discussion on the Mission Playhouse will be held for Council at a later date, and
  thanked the voters who approved Measure SG without whom the City would be
  looking at draconian cuts in the wake of COVID-19 effects.

  The staff presentation was made by Management Specialist Julia James.

  The following members of the public provided comments in support of retaining
  funding for the Historic Preservation Ordinance in the 2020-21 Budget: Senya Lubisich,
  Chair of the Historic Preservation and Cultural Resources Commission and resident;
  Isela Bowles, resident; Camila Lopez, resident; Ashely Hernandez, resident; and Eloy
  Zarate.

  Discussion included commendation to Public Works Director/City Engineer de Vinck
  for the savings realized in Public Works under his direction; transit occupancy tax (TOT)
  calculations; property tax inflow; use of Measure R and Senate Bill (SB) 1/Road
  Maintenance and Rehabilitation Act funds; 2021 estimated gas tax revenue; animal
  control cost increases; funding for the Chamber of Commerce; concern about whether
  revenue estimates are conservative enough; Mission Playhouse event revenue; Other
  Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) Trust contributions; freezing vacant positions for six
  months; various additional cost-savings options not included in the budget; virtual
  events in lieu of traditional events; costs for street maintenance; details of the
  proposed signal-control system; and the public facility maintenance line item
  including a police station addition funded by restricted-use development impact fees.

  Discussion continued on the increase in the amount for insurance premium costs;
  general fund spending required for certain projects before gas tax funds kick in;
  savings and other benefits for using in-house staff rather than consultants for Public
  Works projects; elements that may be included for the street infrastructure budget
  amount; Metro project-funding, timing, and functionality details; cell tower
  considerations; frequency of future budget reviews; prioritization when filling staff
  positions; the need for an agreement with the Chamber of Commerce if funding is
  continued; the desire to continue funding for the Historic Preservation Ordinance; and
  future discussions on funding for the retirement fund, street improvements, new Police
  facility, and Mission Playhouse during development of the next strategic plan.

3. ADJOURNMENT
